article.headline: Central Texas braces for 4-6 inches of rain as flooding risk peaks Thursday
article.summary: A Flood Watch covering most of Central Texas through Friday evening brings multiple rounds of storms with 2-4 inches of rain expected, rising to 4-6 inches in isolated areas, with the highest flooding risk on Thursday.
article.body:
Central Texas faces a moderate to high risk of street, flash, and river flooding on Thursday as tropical moisture collides with a slow-moving front and low pressure system to fuel multiple rounds of downpours. Most of Central Texas is under a Flood Watch from Wednesday evening through Friday evening, according to FOX 7 Austin.

The forecast danger peaks Thursday with two distinct storm rounds. The first arrives early in the day with scattered storms and moderate rain, while a second round of widespread heavy rain and strong storms follows late Thursday, bringing the main flooding concern along with small hail and gusty winds. The slow-moving front will focus storm development, and upper-level lift will keep storms strong throughout the period.

Rainfall totals of 2-4 inches are expected across the region, but isolated areas will receive 4-6 inches. Where the highest totals occur remains the biggest forecasting challenge. North Texas faces a similar multi-day wet pattern, with a separate Flood Watch extended through 7 a.m. Friday, bringing widespread totals of 2-4 inches and isolated amounts of 5-6 inches, according to FOX 4 News Dallas-Fort Worth. The exceptionally dry ground in the North Texas region will increase rapid runoff and localized flooding risk, especially where storms train over the same areas overnight and into Thursday morning.

A cold front will move through Friday, bringing relief from the unseasonable heat with highs dropping into the upper 70s and lower 80s by late week.

article.headline: Disruptive passenger triggers 2-hour delay, passengers applaud as woman exits Scoot flight
article.summary: A woman was removed from Scoot flight TR905 in Macau on September 27 for disruptive behaviour, causing a two-hour delay before the plane departed for Singapore with 173 passengers.
article.body:
As the woman was led off the aircraft by police and flight attendants, passengers applauded in the background. She raised her hands with peace signs while being escorted down the aisle by at least four security personnel.

The disruption cost the flight significantly: flight TR905 was scheduled to depart Macau for Singapore at 6.45pm local time but did not leave until 8.46pm. According to Scoot, the delay stemmed from the time required to remove the disruptive passenger, wait for local authorities to arrive, and offload her checked baggage. All 173 other passengers remained on the aircraft and were served refreshments during the two-hour wait.

Scoot handed the passenger over to local authorities at Macau International Airport but did not disclose what disturbance she had caused on board. The Straits Times reported the incident occurred on October 1, while other sources place the flight on September 27 and the video posting on September 28. Investigations into the incident are ongoing, Scoot said, unable to provide further details. The airline apologised and stated that "the safety and well-being of our customers and crew are our top priority and we will take appropriate measures against any passenger who poses a risk to them."

article.headline: Perth Police Snatch Power to Ban Protesters From Defence Expo Fort
article.summary: Western Australian police are enforcing a strict security zone at next week's Land Forces expo, with letters already issued banning specific individuals from the site.
article.body:
Letters delivered to at least six people this week warn that entering the designated security zone around the Perth Convention and Exhibition Centre will result in arrest, a maximum of three years in prison, and fines up to $36,000. These restrictions are part of a fortified security operation that includes the use of facial recognition technology to track those on an exclusion list. Protesters who remain on the list are legally required to stay outside the perimeter, which covers the exhibition centre and the Elizabeth Quay bus port.

These measures represent a significant shift in event management for Western Australia, as the state government aims to avoid the violent clashes that occurred during the 2024 Land Forces expo in Melbourne, where 24 police officers were injured by protesters throwing items including rocks and acid. To facilitate the event, which runs from October 6 to 8 and is expected to host 20,000 delegates, the government has allocated $11.5 million for enhanced security.

Under new legislation passed last month, police now possess broad temporary powers until October 10. Within the security zone, officers are authorized to stop, search, and evict any person, as well as remove face coverings. The list of items police can confiscate is extensive, ranging from speakers and microphones to dangerous insects like bees, flares, and bottles. While Commander Darren Seivwright confirmed the operation creates a secure fort, groups including the Greens and the WA Anti-War Collective have criticized the police for a lack of transparency regarding the criteria for the bans.

The security zone remains in effect until October 10 to cover the full duration of the event, including the setup and final pack-down phases.

article.headline: Trump adviser tells Canadian lobbyists to 'get the hell out' of U.S.
article.summary: Peter Navarro, a trade adviser to President Trump, warned Canadian lobbyists on Tuesday to leave the U.S. and threatened repercussions if Canada interferes in upcoming midterm elections.
article.body:
Peter Navarro, one of U.S. President Donald Trump's trade advisers, issued a direct threat to Canada during remarks at an economic conference in Washington on Tuesday. "Memo to Canada: You cannot do that," Navarro said, telling Canadian lobbyists on K Street—Washington's hub for lobbying firms—to "get the hell out of our country" and warning that "if you interfere in our elections in Maine or Michigan you will pay even more dearly."

Navarro's comments signal escalating friction over Canada's approach to U.S. trade policy. He criticized Ottawa's strategy of leaning on American labor and business groups to influence negotiations, a tactic Canada used during talks that led to the Canada-U.S.-Mexico Agreement in Trump's first term. Since Trump returned to the White House in early 2025, Canadian provinces have also hired representatives to advocate for their interests during ongoing trade discussions in Washington.

The tensions come as a U.S. ban on certain Canadian imports took effect at midnight on Tuesday, affecting key industries including alcohol, dairy, and motorcycles. Trump signed the executive order in response to Canada's retaliatory tariffs following the collapse of trade talks in August. The White House justified the measure by saying Canada's restrictions on U.S. alcohol, autos, and dairy products put American exporters at a disadvantage.

When asked about Navarro's remarks at a press conference in Vancouver, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney laughed and said he had "no response" to the warning. Navarro said he "loves" the Canadian people but has harbored no goodwill toward Canadian negotiators since 2016.

article.headline: Luke Woodhouse stuns world number one Luke Littler at World Grand Prix
article.summary: Defending champion Luke Littler suffered a 2-1 first-round loss to Luke Woodhouse on Monday at the 2026 World Grand Prix in Leicester.
article.body:
World number one Luke Littler saw his World Grand Prix title defense end in the opening round after a 2-1 defeat by Luke Woodhouse. The 19-year-old opened the match by winning the first set 3-1, including a 106 checkout on double 15. However, Woodhouse rallied to win the second set and held his nerve on a double 16 in the decider to force a final set. Woodhouse moved 2-0 ahead in the last set and sealed the victory on double 12, with both players averaging near 82.50 across the match.

For followers of the Professional Darts Corporation, the tournament remains a high-stakes event with a total prize fund of £750,000, representing a 25% increase from the previous year. The tournament is unique for its 'double in, double out' format, which has been in place since 1998 and requires players to start every leg on a double. The winner of the overall event stands to take home £150,000, up from the £120,000 awarded in 2025.

According to The Guardian, this result comes following a week of scrutiny for Littler, who recently faced negative crowd reactions during a tournament in the Netherlands. Despite the loss, the world number one publicly congratulated Woodhouse on his performance via social media. The field for this year's competition comprises 32 players, including the top 16 ranked in the PDC Order of Merit and 16 others who qualified over the past 12 months.

Woodhouse now advances to the last 16 stage of the tournament. He is scheduled to face Nathan Aspinall, who reached this round by defeating Kevin Doets 2-1. The event continues in Leicester as the remaining competitors vie for the increased prize purse.

article.headline: Portugal Snatches 4-2 Victory Over Denmark In Life After Cristiano Ronaldo
article.summary: Portugal maintained their perfect Nations League start by defeating Denmark 4-2 in Copenhagen as Vitinha and Joao Felix secured late goals.
article.body:
Vitinha celebrated his first ever international goal with a header while Joao Felix added a late strike to help Portugal overcome Denmark 4-2, maintaining a perfect record in Nations League Group A4. The victory arrived just days after 41-year-old Cristiano Ronaldo left the national team camp following a tenure on the bench during a previous match against Norway.

This outcome signifies a potential shift in the national team's tactical approach under head coach Jorge Jesus. By securing a win without the record-holding forward, the squad demonstrated a transition toward a team-oriented structure, with Jesus emphasizing that internal rules remain identical for every player regardless of their individual status or history.

Joao Cancelo opened the scoring for Portugal in the 13th minute before Mikkel Damsgaard equalized for the hosts. Gonçalo Ramos regained the lead for the visitors after 25 minutes, though Rasmus Højlund leveled the score at 2-2 early in the second half. The match remained tense until the final stages when Portugal's attacking depth ultimately overwhelmed the Danish defense. Ronaldo, who has recorded 146 goals and 234 caps for his country, departed the setup after reports emerged of a disagreement with his former club manager, Jorge Jesus. 

Portugal will look to continue their momentum in the group stage following this performance, which the coaching staff characterized as a performance of high standard. The match also drew attention for the atmosphere surrounding the team, with Ronaldo’s departure serving as a major talking point in international football circles.

article.headline: SASSA Flags 169,000 Social Grant Beneficiaries for Potential Fraudulent Transactions
article.summary: The South African Social Security Agency has flagged 169,000 beneficiaries for further investigation after they failed to appear for mandatory grant reviews.
article.body:
A total of 169,000 grant recipients ignored notices to appear for eligibility reviews, resulting in their accounts being marked for potential fraud investigations. This massive audit is part of a wider effort by the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) to verify the status of 352,000 beneficiaries throughout the 2026/27 financial year.

These reviews serve as a critical gatekeeper for public funds, ensuring that assistance reaches only those currently entitled to it. For many recipients, failing to update contact details or neglecting the 90-day review window risks an immediate loss of financial support. While the agency aims to prevent waste, the scale of the flagged cases underscores the difficulty in maintaining accurate beneficiary records across the country.

Minister of Social Development Dina Pule stated that these investigations address instances where eligibility has changed, cases of payments continuing after a beneficiary’s death, and accounts linked to untraceable individuals. In the first quarter alone, SASSA reviewed 105,600 files. Of those, 56,807 grants were initially suspended due to non-compliance, though 5,231 of those cases were later reinstated once the recipients complied with the verification requirements.

Risk-based data analysis continues for the remainder of the fiscal year, with specific targets set for each province. SASSA officials confirmed that while Child Support Grant reviews were prioritized in the first batch, further assessments regarding Disability and Older Persons Grants are currently being determined.

article.headline: Steelers trade cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys after failed contract extension talks
article.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers traded cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys on Wednesday after the two sides could not reach a contract extension agreement, with Porter in the final year of his rookie deal at a $4.9 million cap hit.
article.body:
Joey Porter Jr. has not played a snap this season for Pittsburgh, sitting out the first three games after being placed on the reserve/non-injury list in early August with a back injury that many believed masked a deeper contractual dispute.

For the Steelers, the trade represents a reset after months of failed negotiations. General manager Omar Khan had stated in late August that the franchise would not negotiate extensions during the season, and no deal materialized before Pittsburgh's Week 1 deadline. Steelers coach Mike McCarthy acknowledged the two sides were at an "impasse" in talks. Porter, drafted 32nd overall in 2023, wanted compensation matching top-tier cornerbacks—Christian Gonzalez signed a four-year, $135 million deal this offseason and Devon Witherspoon a four-year, $132 million contract—but Pittsburgh declined to match those figures.

For Dallas, the trade accelerates the Cowboys' defensive overhaul. The team started last season by acquiring Kenny Clark and Quinnen Williams, then added Rashan Gary before the draft. The secondary has struggled early this season after losing Cobie Durant to injury, and Dallas enters the trade with a 1-2 record. Adding Porter addresses that weakness as the franchise attempts to improve pass protection.

Porter's three-year NFL resume includes 165 combined tackles, 3 interceptions, and 31 passes defended. Last season he appeared in 14 games with 52 tackles, one sack, one interception, and 14 passes defended. His father, Joey Porter, played linebacker in the NFL from 1999 to 2011 with Pittsburgh, Miami, and Arizona.

article.headline: Green ID book production ends March 31, 2027, then banned next year
article.summary: South Africa's Home Affairs Minister announced the green ID book will stop being produced on March 31, 2027, and will no longer be valid identification from March 31, 2028, as the government shifts to the more secure Smart ID card.
article.body:
The green ID book's 12-month countdown to obsolescence begins when production shuts down on 31 March 2027. From 31 March 2028, the document will no longer be recognised as valid identification, giving millions of South Africans a year to switch to the Smart ID card or the newly demonstrated digital ID credential.

Home Affairs Minister Leon Schreiber cited security as the driving force. Independent research found the green ID book is among Africa's most fraud-prone identity documents because it relies on paper and manual photographs that can be manipulated. Schreiber said the document "sits at the core of the scourge of identity theft in the country" and enables the production of fraudulent papers, including those used by people seeking illegal South African documentation.

On the same day Schreiber announced the green ID deadline, he demonstrated South Africa's first working digital ID on his smartphone, using the MyMzansi app and his thumbprint to confirm his identity. The digital credential displays the photograph from the population register rather than a model image. Director-general Tommy Makhode tested the system by requesting Schreiber's citizenship details; Schreiber generated a QR code that Makhode scanned, then selectively shared his nationality while blocking his ID number. The digital ID is set to be voluntary, though no launch date has been announced.

article.headline: Japan and Ecuador Clash at Yokohama Stadium in 2026 Kirin Cup
article.summary: Japan faces Ecuador in the 2026 Kirin Cup semifinal on October 1 at Nissan Stadium in Yokohama.
article.body: The match kicks off at 7:10 p.m. JST, marking a significant test for both nations following the 2026 FIFA World Cup. While the encounter serves as a competitive semifinal for the Kirin Cup, it also highlights international cultural connections, as Ecuador has unveiled a special-edition yellow jersey for the event. This unique kit features red line-art graphics depicting an Andean condor facing a Japanese red-crowned crane, symbolizing a duel between the cultural icons of both countries. The jersey includes dark navy trims on the collar and sleeve cuffs, maintaining the team's traditional yellow aesthetic while serving as part of a bespoke series for the Asian tour. The kit follows a similar collector's edition white jersey worn against South Korea one week prior. For fans following the action, Japan’s starting lineup includes Suzuki, Itakura, Seko, Ito, Doan, Sano, Tanaka, Nakamura, Kubo, Y. Suzuki, and Tanimura. Ecuador counters with a lineup featuring Galindez, Alcivar, Pacho, Estupinan, Yeboah, Arroyo, Vite, Angulo, Franco, Mercado, and Porozo. The game is broadcast in Japan via TBS and streaming through TVer, with coverage beginning at 6:30 p.m. Ecuadorian viewers can tune into Teleamazonas or TC Televisión for live coverage of the proceedings.

article.headline: Kenya seeks redemption in Guinea after Eritrea stalemate
article.summary: Kenya's national team faces Guinea on Thursday at 7 pm in Conakry, looking to recover from a 1-1 draw with Eritrea in their Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign.
article.body:
Kenya drew 1-1 with Eritrea in their opening qualifier, a result that frustrated head coach Benni McCarthy despite the performance showing the growing competitiveness of smaller African nations. The draw highlighted that underestimated teams can pose real threats when they are tactically disciplined and dangerous on the counter-attack.

McCarthy's warning to South Africa about respecting Eritrea underscores what Kenya learned firsthand: overlooking opponents in this qualifying round carries real cost. Kenya cannot afford another slow start as they bid to reach the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations. The Guinea match offers an immediate chance to correct course and build momentum in the group stage.

Kenya must now travel to Conakry to face Guinea, a team they hope presents a different challenge than the stubborn Eritrean side. The Harambee Stars need a positive result to stay competitive in their qualifying group and demonstrate they can adapt after the opening stalemate.

article.headline: Justice Department files ethics complaint against 7 Minnesota judges over immigration enforcement comments
article.summary: Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the DOJ filed a judicial misconduct complaint Wednesday against seven federal judges in Minnesota who spoke to the New York Times about government violations of court orders during Operation Metro Surge.
article.body:
The Justice Department took the unusual step of filing a complaint with the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 8th Circuit against judges who publicly discussed their concerns over the Trump administration's immigration enforcement surge. At the center of the dispute is a New York Times article featuring Judge Patrick Schiltz, who gave a 90-minute interview describing what he said were repeated violations of court orders by the government. Schiltz, nominated by President George W. Bush and a former law clerk to Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia, accused the government in January of failing to comply with nearly 100 court orders and wrote in a ruling that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement "is not a law unto itself."

Attorney General Todd Blanche argued the judges violated judicial ethics and showed bias in their remarks. "When we have a situation like we have now, where you have a judge, a couple of judges, just not only violating the canons in our view, but also showing bias in what they're saying, we have no choice but to act to defend not only our prosecutors, but also DHS," Blanche said at a press conference.

The complaint names Schiltz and Judge John Tunheim, nominated by President Bill Clinton, along with anonymous district judges serving on the U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota. Six of the seven members of Minnesota's federal bench spoke with the New York Times about Operation Metro Surge, which led to thousands of arrests in the Twin Cities during last winter.

The DOJ is demanding the judges recuse themselves from all criminal and civil cases involving the Department of Homeland Security. However, a Minnesota federal court spokesperson told the Associated Press that legal experts have stated the judges acted "well within the ethical rules that apply to federal judges" in their comments to the newspaper.

article.headline: KFC jumps 30% bigger on chicken tenders after complaints of dry, scrawny rivals
article.summary: KFC relaunched larger, crispier chicken tenders this week after a surge in complaints and lost sales to competitors, marking the first step in its biggest menu overhaul in decades.
article.body:
Over 18 months, a team of chefs developed tenders that are 30 percent bigger and crispier than before, responding to what KFC senior innovation development manager Kathryn Lake called "a high number of complaints about them." The relaunch comes as fast-food rivals like El Jannah, Guzman y Gomez, and Wingstop have chipped into KFC's customer base with their own fried and boneless chicken offerings, spurring customer complaints and a drop-off in sales.

Vanessa Rowed, chief marketing officer at Yum! Brands (which operates KFC in Australia), said the old tenders felt too small and dry. "We didn't have the best tenders in the market," she told the Australian Financial Review. The new version achieves crispiness and juiciness through a change in how they are cooked.

The tenders come at a higher price: a three-pack bundle rose from $9.45 to $10.95, and a five-pack from $12.95 to $14.95. Rowed signaled the overhaul extends beyond tenders. "We're going to set the benchmark here and then we're going to do that with every single product in our portfolio," she said, though she stopped short of confirming changes to KFC's bestselling Original Recipe, developed by Colonel Harland Sanders in 1940.

The shift reflects a broader industry pivot toward chicken as a menu centerpiece across Australian fast food, with chains like Hungry Jack's launching Jack's Fried Chicken in 2021 and McDonald's introducing the McCrispy in 2023.

article.headline: Minimum wage surges in 5 provinces as pay rates climb nationwide
article.summary: Ontario, Prince Edward Island, Nova Scotia, Manitoba and Saskatchewan hiked minimum hourly wages on October 1, 2026.
article.body:
While Nunavut continues to lead Canada with a minimum wage exceeding $20 per hour, workers in five other provinces saw pay bumps ranging from 25 to 40 cents as of October 1, 2026. This latest adjustment leaves Alberta as the only province that has not increased its base pay rate since 2019, keeping it at the country's lowest level of $15 an hour. 

For roughly 700,000 workers in Ontario alone, the new $17.95 rate represents an annual increase of approximately $728 for those working 40 hours per week. Officials state these adjustments are tied to the Consumer Price Index to help families manage rising costs of living, international trade uncertainty, and shifting labour market demands. 

Despite the increases, critics suggest the new rates fail to bridge the gap between government-mandated minimums and the actual costs of living. Anne Coleman of the Ontario Living Wage Network noted that the current living wage in the Greater Toronto Area sits at $27.20 an hour, nearly $10 above the updated provincial minimum. She emphasized that rental and food expenses are currently rising faster than general inflation, making it difficult for minimum wage earners to pay their monthly bills. 

Nova Scotia’s move to $17 per hour follows a unanimous recommendation from the province's Minimum Wage Review Committee. The adjustment process in Nova Scotia is calculated based on the consumer price index plus one per cent. Similar adjustments are now in effect across Prince Edward Island at $17.30, Manitoba at $16.40, and Saskatchewan at $15.70. With these changes, every Canadian province and territory has successfully increased its minimum wage rate within the 2026 calendar year.

article.headline: Watson's 2-win streak ends reevaluation talk at Cleveland after 2-1 start
article.summary: Deshaun Watson has led the Cleveland Browns to back-to-back victories following an opening loss, shifting the team's short-term plans away from week-to-week quarterback changes.
article.body:
Watson's ability to move past negative plays instead of compounding them has stood out to team sources, marking a significant shift in how the Browns view their 31-year-old quarterback. After years of being viewed as a liability, Watson is producing results that have changed the conversation inside the building.

The Browns' surprising 2-1 start matters because it affects how the team will manage its quarterback position going forward. Team sources indicated Watson's performance through three games hasn't convinced Cleveland he's the long-term answer, but the momentum has altered near-term strategy. Watson is no longer being evaluated on a week-to-week basis after the Browns initially planned to reevaluate the quarterback position following Week 2.

Watson's path to stability came after a season-opening loss to Jacksonville. He then led the Browns to back-to-back victories at Tampa Bay and against Carolina—his first consecutive wins in Cleveland since 2023. The quarterback made his return this season after tearing his Achilles tendon in 2024, beating out Shedeur Sanders for the Week 1 starting job in training camp. Watson signed a fully-guaranteed five-year, $230 million contract in 2022 and is in the final year of that deal.

The Browns face Pittsburgh in Week 4 on Thursday Night Football. While Watson may not be the long-term solution—Cleveland likely wants to develop a rookie quarterback for future contention—the short-term momentum suggests the team and Watson will continue building together.

article.headline: Malaysia Routs Singapore 6-0 to End Lions' FIFA ASEAN Cup Campaign
article.summary: Singapore suffered a historic 6-0 defeat against Malaysia at the Si Jalak Harupat Stadium on October 1, eliminating the Lions from the FIFA ASEAN Cup.
article.body:
Singapore experienced a crushing end to their inaugural FIFA ASEAN Cup campaign on October 1, falling 6-0 to their Causeway rivals, Malaysia, in Bandung. The result marked Singapore’s heaviest defeat at a senior level since 1978, when they lost to Malaysia by the same margin. Brazil-born striker Bergson led the offensive for Malaysia with a hat-trick, supported by additional goals from Stuart Wilkin, Paulo Josue, and Syahir Bashah.

This lopsided scoreline serves as a significant reality check for coach Gavin Lee’s side, particularly with the Asian Cup approaching in three months. While Singapore entered the match with three points after an earlier 1-0 win over Bangladesh, they were unable to contain Malaysia’s attack. Coach Lee acknowledged the disappointment after the game, stating that his team failed to do enough to qualify and must now reflect on the performance levels required for future competitions.

Following the victory, Malaysia finished second in Group A behind Indonesia. Despite the emphatic win, Malaysia fell short of securing the top spot due to a lower goal tally compared to the hosts. Indonesia secured their place in the final with a 9-2 victory over Bangladesh. Malaysia is now expected to face Vietnam in the Division 1 third-place play-off on October 5, while the group winners, Indonesia, prepare to challenge Thailand for the tournament title.

Singapore concludes the group stage in third place with three points. The squad now turns its attention to long-term preparation, as the team looks to move forward after this defeat.

article.headline: Emirates Airbus A380 diverts to Frankfurt after mid-air passenger medical emergency
article.summary: Emirates flight EK31 from Dubai to London Heathrow made an emergency landing at Frankfurt Airport on Thursday after a passenger required medical attention.
article.body:
Six hours into a 7-hour and 20-minute flight, the crew of the double-decker Airbus A380-800 transmitted the international transponder code Squawk 7700 while cruising at 40,000 feet. The aircraft initiated a rapid descent over European airspace, shifting its course from London Heathrow to Frankfurt to address the unfolding situation.

The diversion serves as a direct response to a health crisis on board, with Emirates confirming that the cabin crew provided assistance while the plane was in the air. For the hundreds of passengers on the flight, the unscheduled stop meant an abrupt change in travel plans, though the airline has since worked to rebook connecting flights and provide updated itineraries for those affected.

According to Emirates, the aircraft landed safely in Frankfurt, where the passenger disembarked to receive further medical support. While flight tracking data initially identified the alert as a general emergency, the airline subsequently clarified the specific nature of the event. The carrier issued an apology to customers, stating that the health and safety of both passengers and crew remains its highest priority.

Following the landing, the airline coordinated a recovery leg to transport remaining passengers to their original destination. Emirates scheduled the aircraft to depart Frankfurt for London Heathrow at 17:30 local time, with a projected arrival at London Heathrow shortly thereafter.

article.headline: WhatsApp gives parents power to monitor teens' group activity and privacy settings
article.summary: WhatsApp is rolling out optional parental controls that let guardians see when teenagers join or leave groups and decide privacy settings, though message content remains encrypted.
article.body:
WhatsApp is giving parents new tools to oversee their teenagers' activity on the messaging app, including notifications when a teen joins or leaves a group and alerts when a group their child is in grows meaningfully in size. Parents can also control who sees their child's profile photo, who can add them to groups, and how they use Channels.

The move responds to pressure on tech companies to create safer experiences for young users. Meta, which owns WhatsApp, faces regulatory scrutiny over child safety. The controls are designed to help parents guide teenagers on responsible app use while keeping messages and calls protected by end-to-end encryption—parents cannot read their child's conversations or calls, according to WhatsApp's blog post.

Parents set up the controls using a PIN that teenagers need to enter if they want to disable them. The settings are optional and can be adjusted or switched off at any time. Teens can relax any restrictions with parental approval through the PIN system. WhatsApp noted that once parents and teens update the app, the parental control option becomes available in settings.

Social media analyst Matt Navarra called the optional nature an "obvious weakness," noting the feature's success depends on whether families actually use it. He said Meta is attempting to demonstrate to regulators that it has child safety systems in place, though the big question remains whether enough families will adopt the controls.

article.headline: Suzuki beat Miller's slider for walk-off; Padres' closer eyes revenge in playoff rematch
article.summary: Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki hit a walk-off single off San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller on a slider in June, but the two face off again Tuesday in the Wild Card Series with the Cubs' season at stake.
article.body:
Seiya Suzuki has already solved Mason Miller once this year, and now he may get another chance to do it when it counts most. On June 29 at Wrigley Field, Suzuki faced Miller with two outs and the score tied 2-2 in the ninth inning. Miller had entered after two Cubs reached base, and a double play at the plate had nearly ended Chicago's chance. Suzuki drove a slider toward left-field ivy for a walk-off single, scoring Crow-Armstrong for a 3-2 victory.

Miller's regular-season dominance suggests that single may prove the exception rather than the rule. The Padres closer finished the season with 38 saves, establishing himself as one of baseball's most dominant ninth-inning pitchers. His 102.9 mph fastball has overpowered most hitters, including Suzuki in last year's playoffs.

The Cubs will open their Wild Card Series against the Padres on Tuesday at Petco Park, with Michael King starting for San Diego but Miller likely taking over in crucial late-inning situations. Suzuki's June success came when he specifically looked for a slider while remaining aware of Miller's triple-digit fastball. He let the first slider go above the zone, then drove the next one that came over the heart of the plate. Whether Miller repeats that mistake remains unclear, but their rematch could prove decisive with Chicago's season hanging in the balance.

article.headline: Piastri's brake lock-up in Azerbaijan drops him from podium to points-free horror
article.summary: Oscar Piastri locked up on lap 40 of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, plummeting from third place to 14th and out of the points in what he called a surprising moment that extended his difficult 2026 season.
article.body:
Piastri held second place through the opening corner of the Baku race, overtaking Charles Leclerc and holding off Max Verstappen's early pressure. He maintained position through the first safety car restart but lost ground to Verstappen before a second safety car reset the field. On the 40th lap, defending his third position against Isack Hadjar at Turn 1, both of Piastri's front brakes locked up simultaneously, sending him off the track and down the order in a single moment.

The incident wiped out what would have been Piastri's first podium since Miami in May. Instead of scoring points, he finished 14th, his second consecutive race without a result. McLaren scored no points in Azerbaijan, with teammate Lando Norris also failing to score after a collision at the opening corner.

Piastri said the lock-up "certainly took me by surprise," telling reporters he did not brake late or hard before both fronts locked. "I didn't think I braked super late or super hard – just instantly locked both fronts, so I need to look at that," he said, noting he would review the data to understand whether a bump in the road or another factor caused the failure.

The setback extends Piastri's difficult 2026 season, in which he has scored just two podiums so far. Norris has taken two wins in the previous five races, widening the gap between the teammates.

article.headline: Abdul Samad smashes 22 off five balls as Pakistan reach first Asian Games cricket final
article.summary: Pakistan defeated Bangladesh by six wickets on October 1 to reach their maiden Asian Games cricket final, where they will face India on October 3 for the gold medal.
article.body:
Abdul Samad's explosive 22 runs off just five balls in the 10th over turned the semi-final decisively Pakistan's way. The match was effectively decided in that single over, bowled by Bangladesh's Mustafizur Rahman, when Pakistan still needed 36 runs from 24 balls.

Pakistan's place in their first-ever Asian Games cricket final ends a long wait for the men's team. They will now face world champions India on October 3 for the gold medal, after India dismantled Sri Lanka by 124 runs in the other semi-final on the same day.

Bangladesh had posted 111-7 after Pakistan asked them to bat on a heavily cracked pitch at Korogi Athletic Park Stadium in Nagoya. Pakistan's bowlers had Bangladesh reeling at 21-3 and then 45-4 in the sixth over. Towhid Hridoy led a recovery with 42 off 25 balls with two fours and four sixes. Pakistan lost three early wickets chasing quick runs but recovered from 53-4 when Samad and Hasan Nawaz came together. The pair posted an unbroken 59-run stand in 32 balls as Pakistan cruised home with nine balls to spare.

Pakistan batsman Saim Ayub, who scored 21, said: "All we care about is winning the final, no matter who we are playing against."

article.headline: Danny Boyle backs Jack O'Connell for next James Bond role
article.summary: Director Danny Boyle endorsed actor Jack O'Connell as the next James Bond during a masterclass at the Zurich Film Festival, praising his ability to make audiences root for morally complex characters.
article.body:
At the Zurich Film Festival, Danny Boyle made his pitch for the next 007: Jack O'Connell. The 28 Years Later director, who was once attached to direct Bond 25 before it became No Time To Die, believes O'Connell has the range to carry the spy franchise. Boyle highlighted O'Connell's performance in the 2024 film Ink, where he plays Larry Lamb, a British tabloid editor, describing how the actor makes audiences remain invested in a character whose moral conscience dissolves entirely as he pursues success.

Boyle's endorsement carries weight given his experience with Bond films. He drew comparisons between O'Connell's work in Ink and Al Pacino's performance in The Godfather Part II, suggesting the actor possesses the complexity needed for the iconic role. The director also referenced O'Connell's recent work in the Amy Winehouse biopic Back To Black, calling it "an incredible performance" in "an impossible part."

The casting search for the next James Bond has stretched on as Amazon pursues the rights to the franchise. Boyle's public endorsement adds O'Connell's name to a growing list of candidates who have been suggested for the role, which requires an actor capable of handling both the action and the psychological depth the character demands.

During the same festival appearance, Boyle confirmed that the third film in the 28 Years Later trilogy will be made, with a script by Alex Garland already completed, though timing remains uncertain.

article.body: The Primary School Leaving Examination, or PSLE, has concluded for students across Singapore, but one Primary 6 pupil faced a final hurdle at home. Senior Minister of State for Social and Family Development Goh Pei Ming, currently traveling for work, left a handwritten note on his son’s laptop upon his return from the exam period. The note contained a specific six-digit PIN challenge inspired by a math question from this year’s national testing cycle, effectively turning the boy’s first day of freedom back into a study session to earn his digital privileges back. The minister noted that he was unable to be present in person for the final paper, but expressed pride in his son’s resilience throughout the year. The playful math problem asked the boy to calculate the minimum number of days spent resisting laptop use to reach a total of more than 90 hours of revision, based on a 25-day study window. Beyond this specific family milestone, the national examination remains a focal point in Singaporean life. While the Ministry of Education has implemented policy changes over recent years—such as the removal of PSLE T-scores and the elimination of weighted assessments—a survey by the Institute of Policy Studies indicates that parental stress and spending on tuition and enrichment classes remain elevated compared to a decade ago. Education experts and observers continue to examine the pressures surrounding the system, highlighting how academic milestones like the PSLE contribute to a broader environment of anxiety for students and families. As the written examination period for 2024 finished on September 30, the student now joins thousands of peers awaiting their results, following oral components held on August 12 and 13.

article.headline: Four celebrity pairs race 7,500 km from Borneo to Melbourne Australia
article.summary: The fourth series of the BAFTA-winning show features four new celebrity duos racing from Borneo to Melbourne on a strict daily budget.
article.body:
The participants will traverse 7,500 km starting from the city of Kuching in North West Borneo and ending at the finish line in Melbourne, Australia. Each of the four pairs must survive on a tight budget of just £26 per person a day, navigating through prehistoric jungles and five check points across three countries and two continents without the use of phones, credit cards, or flights.

This grueling adventure matters to viewers as it strips away the VIP lifestyle, forcing household names to rely entirely on local transport, maps, and the kindness of strangers. The experience is designed to test emotional resilience and transform relationships as contestants trade home comforts for an environment where they must manage their own resourcefulness to progress in the race.

According to the BBC, the official line-up features Brit award-winning singer Ella Eyre and her childhood friend Nana, sports broadcaster Jeff Stelling and his son Matt, influencer Princess Andre with her musician brother Junior Andre, and singer Sam Ryder with his tour manager Kaz. The series, produced by Studio Lambert, is set to air on BBC One and BBC iPlayer.

The broadcaster teased the line-up with images of the contestants being photobombed by wild animals. The show is expected to start later this year, with no VIP treatment for any of the participants during their journey.

article.headline: Sperm whale smashes yacht hull, forcing four sailors into desperate sea rescue
article.summary: Four sailors were rescued after their 52-foot yacht, the Tai Tam, sank following a collision with a pod of sperm whales in the South Pacific.
article.body:
The impact was powerful enough to knock Australian Jemma Cooper from the steering wheel of the 52-foot Tai Tam yacht as a pod of six to eight sperm whales surrounded the vessel. Crew member Jeremy Cooper recalled the terrifying moment the boat was shoved sideways, followed by the sight of brown water and several whales lingering near their damaged ship. The collision occurred 250 to 500 nautical miles off the coast of New Zealand, leaving the yacht with a compromised fiberglass structure, shattered steering gear, and water rapidly flooding the hull. 

For the four individuals aboard, the incident meant an immediate shift from sailing to a survival mission on the open ocean. After activating an emergency beacon at 1 p.m. New Zealand time on Saturday, the crew spent several hours frantically bailing water to keep the vessel afloat. The Royal New Zealand Air Force deployed a P-8A Poseidon patrol plane to coordinate the response, while the crew eventually abandoned their sinking yacht for a life raft. 

Survival on the high seas lasted 18 hours until a passing container ship successfully retrieved the group. French crew member Martin Jaffre noted that the loss of steering made the boat unmanageable, sealing its fate as it eventually went under. Despite the harrowing experience of being stranded in a life raft after their ship was destroyed, the Cooper couple has already expressed their intention to return to sailing. The rescue operation highlights the extreme danger posed by deep-sea encounters with marine wildlife, turning a routine transit into a life-or-death crisis in the remote South Pacific.

article.headline: Crew-13 blasts off from Florida to reach the International Space Station
article.summary: Four astronauts successfully launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Kennedy Space Center at 11:10 a.m. Thursday.
article.body:
The mission successfully cleared the launchpad at 11:10 a.m. despite earlier morning uncertainty regarding local weather conditions, which had initially been forecast with only a 60% probability of launch viability. Once the Falcon 9 cleared the atmosphere, the first-stage booster completed a successful touchdown at Landing Zone 40 following stage separation.

This mission is significant as it carries a multinational team to the International Space Station to conduct critical scientific investigations and technology demonstrations. According to NASA, these efforts are specifically designed to support the agency's long-term objectives in preparing human explorers for upcoming missions to both the Moon and Mars.

The four-person crew includes NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, who serve as the spacecraft’s commander and pilot, respectively. Joining them are Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov, both serving as mission specialists. The team spent their final preflight days in quarantine at Kennedy Space Center before Thursday's departure.

Following the successful morning liftoff, the SpaceX Dragon spacecraft is scheduled to dock with the orbital laboratory at approximately 7 p.m. Thursday. NASA will provide continuous coverage of the docking process and subsequent audio-only communications between the crew and ground flight controllers during the transit phase.

article.headline: Kenya Power imposes dumping surcharges on unauthorized residential solar energy grid connections
article.summary: The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority has introduced new fines for homes and businesses feeding excess solar electricity into the grid without approval.
article.body: Wind and solar power accounted for 34 per cent of Kenya’s energy mix during daytime peak demand on August 11, 2026. This reliance on renewable sources has driven regulators to impose stricter oversight on how private systems interact with the national electricity network. Homes and businesses that feed excess solar energy into the Kenya Power network without a valid net-metering agreement or prior authorization now face a formal dumping surcharge. Under the updated 2023 tariff schedule, any electricity exported to the grid without approval is treated as dumping and will be billed at the applicable base tariff. Kenya Power stated these measures are necessary to protect its distribution infrastructure, maintain grid stability, and prevent safety hazards for maintenance staff. Fluctuations in renewable energy generation can impact grid frequency and voltage, which forces the utility company to activate other generators to balance the system. The Energy (Net-Metering) Regulations, 2024, provide a formal framework for consumers with systems up to one megawatt to export surplus power, provided they enter into a legal net-metering agreement. The regulator and Kenya Power retain the authority to disconnect any solar system that threatens the safety, reliability, or security of the distribution network. Moving forward, homeowners and business operators must ensure all connections comply with these established technical and regulatory standards to avoid penalties and potential disconnection from the national supply.

article.headline: Swift Telephone Network clinches licence to challenge Nigeria's telecom market giants
article.summary: Swift Telephone Network Limited has secured a Unified Access Service Licence from the Nigerian Communications Commission to provide nationwide telecommunications services.
article.body:
Starting from humble origins as a table-top calling spot under an umbrella in 1998, Swift Telephone Network Limited has now secured a federal Unified Access Service Licence to compete directly with giants like MTN, Airtel, and Globacom. The company, which faced a complete operational shutdown in November 2010 before being revived by Oluwole Adetuyi in February 2017, marks this regulatory milestone as a definitive return to the national stage. According to the Nigerian Communications Commission, this new licence officially takes effect on October 1, 2026, and is renewable after a decade of operations.

This expansion is significant for Nigeria's digital infrastructure as the company positions itself to provide voice, data, and mobile services. By entering this space, the firm aims to impact the industry by narrowing the digital divide and creating economic opportunities. For the Nigerian telecommunications market, the arrival of another operator signifies a shift toward increased competition in a sector currently dominated by a handful of established international and local players.

STN’s leadership confirmed that the focus is on a business model rooted in Nigeria with global competitive standards. Management plans to emphasize the training of local engineers and digital professionals while forging strategic partnerships with local vendors to build a sustainable value chain. The company previously pioneered digital landline services in Yaba in 2003 and provided essential connectivity for the Nigerian Military and the World Health Organisation.

Looking ahead, the firm plans to release specific details regarding its national rollout strategy and upcoming partnerships in the coming weeks. The company continues to rebuild its infrastructure following years of regulatory reinstatement and economic pivots, transitioning from its previous enterprise-focused model to this broad, mobile-ready mandate.

article.headline: Pro Golfer Phil Mickelson Checks Into Treatment Center for Addiction and Trauma
article.summary: Professional golfer Phil Mickelson voluntarily sought treatment for family trauma and addiction following recent misconduct allegations and personal health issues.
article.body: The 56-year-old golf champion recently entered and completed a stint at an addiction treatment center to address complex personal challenges. A representative for Mickelson confirmed the decision to seek professional help for both addiction and family trauma, noting that the golfer has already been discharged from the facility. This clinical intervention follows a difficult year that saw his private life thrust into the public eye through a series of professional absences and external claims regarding his conduct. In February, Mickelson announced his departure from competition, later clarifying in April that he would miss the Masters tournament to prioritize a family health matter. The decision to enter treatment comes after multiple allegations surfaced against the athlete, including claims by a female golf course employee who reported nonconsensual physical contact. Additionally, Ashley Perez alleged that Mickelson made inappropriate sexual gestures toward her in 2015. Mickelson has publicly labeled these reports as a misleading narrative and described the allegations as a drive-by shooting, while his wife, Amy, has expressed her support throughout the period. Mickelson has previously spoken openly about his history with gambling, admitting in 2023 that his habits had shifted from moderate to addictive, which significantly impacted his personal life. While he has acknowledged some past mistakes, his spokespeople have explicitly denied the more recent accusations of misconduct, stating that many claims are false or distorted. The golfer continues to navigate these personal health and legal matters after stepping away from his professional career earlier this year.

article.headline: Victorian scoops $1.2m TattsLotto win leaving the dentist
article.summary: A Strathbogie Shire man in Victoria won $1,247,390.16 in TattsLotto draw 4715 on Saturday, September 26, after purchasing his ticket from Euroa News and Lotto, learning of his win when an official called while he was driving home from a dental appointment.
article.body:
A Victorian's trip to the dentist turned into a life-changing moment when The Lott called to inform him he had won $1,247,390.16 in Saturday's TattsLotto draw 4715. The shock left him momentarily speechless as he drove home, barely able to believe the news.

The win means significant changes ahead for the man and his family. He plans to help out relatives and purchase a four-wheel drive, though he acknowledged the windfall left him overwhelmed. "I've always dreamt of all the things I'd do if I ever won but it's quite funny, now I feel stumped," he said, deciding to take a few weeks before committing to spending plans.

The winning ticket was a 10-game entry purchased from Euroa News and Lotto on Binney Street in Euroa, about 160 kilometers northeast of Melbourne. Store owner Lorraine Mawson said the sale marked a major milestone. "We're absolutely ecstatic. The last time we sold a division one-winning entry was in 2018," she said. The man was one of five division one winners in the draw, each receiving the same prize amount from the Saturday, September 26 draw.

article.headline: Code-hopper Nawaqanitawase plays final NRL match in Roosters grand final against Knights
article.summary: Sydney Roosters winger Mark Nawaqanitawase will play his last rugby league game in Sunday's grand final against Newcastle Knights before returning to rugby union and the Wallabies.
article.body:
Mark Nawaqanitawase arrived at the Roosters after the Paris 2024 Olympics and made an immediate impact, scoring a try in his round 27 debut and becoming one of the best wingers in the game within two years. But the transition from rugby union to league was mentally brutal: during his first off-season, NRL legend Andrew Johns recalled that Nawaqanitawase confessed he was questioning whether he could continue. "I don't think I can get through it," he told Johns, describing days spent training in the morning before collapsing on the lounge, unable to move. "We train in the morning, and if we have time off I just go home and lay on the lounge. I can't move off the lounge."

By his second year, Nawaqanitawase had adapted completely. When Johns saw him again, the star had adjusted to league's different fitness demands and cemented himself as a genuine superstar. Johns noted the transformation: "my body is used to it now," Nawaqanitawase told him.

Nawaqanitawase's departure marks a significant loss for the Roosters and the NRL. His return to rugby union comes with an eye on representing the Wallabies at the home Rugby World Cup next year. Interestingly, his mother Fiona Tovehi initially "tormented" her son about his move to league, but has now changed her stance and does not want him to leave the NRL.

article.headline: Wike urges Nigeria to vote for leaders sustaining Abuja's infrastructure drive
article.summary: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike called on Nigerians to elect progressive leaders in 2027 who will sustain infrastructure development in Abuja, describing the capital as a symbol of national unity.
article.body:
Nigeria's Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike has called on residents to use the 2027 general elections to vote for leaders capable of sustaining and expanding infrastructure development in Abuja. Wike made the appeal in an Independence Day message marking Nigeria's 66th anniversary, urging voters to choose progressive and visionary leaders who will continue transforming the capital into a world-class city.

The push reflects the administration's focus on infrastructure as central to the capital's future. Wike said the FCT Administration had invested heavily in critical infrastructure, including road construction, drainage systems and solar streetlights, extending development beyond the city centre to remote rural communities. According to him, these projects aim to improve accessibility and address security challenges in communities located far from the city centre.

Wike also emphasized Abuja's symbolic importance to Nigeria. He described the capital as a reflection of national unity, where people from different ethnic, religious and cultural backgrounds live and work together. The minister said the FCT, as the nation's capital, has a responsibility to promote inclusive development and reflect the ideals of a united Nigeria.

The administration's development agenda extends beyond central Abuja to satellite towns and rural areas, with Wike stressing that residents across the territory should benefit from government projects and services. He said the FCT remains committed to creating a modern, inclusive and functional capital that serves all residents.

article.headline: DFI seizes full control of 1,100 Starbucks across Asia, exits Maxim's partnership
article.summary: DFI Retail Group will take sole control of Starbucks operations across seven Asian markets—Singapore, Hong Kong, Macau, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia and Laos—and receive US$340 million in cash by ending its 50-50 joint venture with Hongkong Caterers in Maxim's Caterers.
article.body:
DFI Retail Group is dismantling a longstanding partnership to consolidate power over one of Asia's largest coffee chains. The Singapore-listed company will assume full control of more than 1,100 licensed Starbucks coffeehouses across seven markets, ending a 50-50 joint venture with Hongkong Caterers that has governed Maxim's Caterers since 1972.

The restructuring significantly streamlines DFI's portfolio. The company exits its stake in Maxim's Caterers and relinquishes ownership of international food brands including Genki Sushi, Ippudo, Shake Shack and The Cheesecake Factory, which Maxim's brought into Asia. In exchange, DFI receives approximately US$340 million in cash. Hongkong Caterers becomes the sole owner of the remaining Maxim's business, which operates more than 1,000 outlets across nine markets.

Maxim's Caterers, founded in Hong Kong in 1956 by the Wu family, became the joint venture structure in 1972 with Hongkong Caterers and the Jardine Matheson Group. DFI and Hongkong Caterers stated that day-to-day operations for both Starbucks and Maxim's businesses will remain unchanged during the transition.

The deal was announced by DFI on September 29 and is expected to complete by the end of the first quarter of 2027, subject to standard closing conditions.

article.headline: Only 26.6% of young Brits have taken meningitis B vaccine as outbreaks kill three
article.summary: Health officials warn that hundreds of thousands of eligible young people have not yet received the meningitis B vaccine despite three deaths from recent outbreaks and a one-off NHS vaccination programme launched this summer.
article.body:
Just 212,549 out of 799,840 eligible young people in the UK had received the meningitis B vaccine by September 20, leaving vast numbers unprotected as outbreaks continue. The UK Health Security Agency warned that "similar outbreaks could occur again" after three deaths resulted from meningococcal disease this year, including two in an outbreak of 21 confirmed cases around Canterbury in March 2026.

First-year university students face roughly seven times higher risk of contracting meningococcal disease than young people the same age who do not attend university, according to the UK Health Security Agency. The close contact during freshers' week—from shared accommodation to socialising in pubs and clubs—creates ideal conditions for bacteria spread. Meningococcal disease can develop rapidly and become life-threatening within hours, potentially causing meningitis, sepsis, hearing loss, neurological damage and limb amputation in survivors.

Tiff O'Connor, who contracted meningitis B in her first year at university eight years ago, described the sudden onset of the disease. "My head was a pain that I'd never experienced before," she said. "I truly thought it was going to melt out of my ears." Doctors said her prior vaccination bought her crucial time. She was rushed to intensive care, put into a medically induced coma and treated with ice to lower her temperature while her family were told to say goodbye.

Year 13 pupils and individuals under 25 starting university can access two doses of the MenB vaccine via high street pharmacies and the NHS website. Health officials urged eligible individuals to book both doses as soon as possible, noting that while uptake is "gradually increasing", the large numbers remaining unprotected pose continued risk.

article.headline: Alexander Zverev Topples Cameron Norrie in Beijing After Missed Break Point Opportunity
article.summary: Cameron Norrie exited the ATP Beijing Open in the first round following a defeat against Alexander Zverev.
article.body:
Cameron Norrie let a pivotal opportunity slip through his fingers during his opening match at the China Open. The Brit fell to Alexander Zverev as he failed to capitalize on crucial chances to shift the momentum in his favor. Despite entering the contest with the aim of advancing on the hard courts of Beijing, Norrie struggled to contain his opponent's clinical approach when the pressure reached its peak. 

For tennis fans and followers of the ATP tour, the match highlights the punishing nature of high-stakes competition where a single missed opportunity can decide the outcome of an entire tie. Zverev’s ability to remain composed under pressure served as a stark contrast to the missed windows Norrie faced throughout the encounter. This result marks an early exit for the British player at the tournament, which attracts some of the world's best athletes to compete simultaneously across both professional tours. 

The event in Beijing, known for its unique atmosphere and competitive slate of matches, continues into its second day of play. According to The Independent, Norrie was ultimately punished for failing to convert those key moments, allowing Zverev to control the flow of the game. With the field narrowed, attention now shifts to the remaining players participating in the first-round fixtures as they look to build momentum for the rest of the event. While players like Andrey Rublev and Tallon Griekspoor prepare for their own clashes, the early departure of Norrie leaves a gap in the draw, as the remaining competitors now aim to navigate the demanding hard-court surface.

article.headline: Taran Armstrong Dagger Clinches 84-82 JackJumpers Thriller Over Melbourne United
article.summary: Burnie-born Taran Armstrong drilled a game-winning jump shot with 5.5 seconds remaining to secure a two-point victory for the Tasmania JackJumpers on Thursday night.
article.body: Burnie-born point guard Taran Armstrong delivered a clutch pull-up jumper with just 5.5 seconds remaining to break an 82-82 deadlock at Hobart's MyState Bank Arena. After Melbourne United’s Sam Waardenburg hit a three-pointer to level the score with 14.2 seconds on the clock, Tasmania responded with a time-out before Armstrong’s decisive shot. United had a final opportunity to steal the game, but Malith Machar’s long-range attempt rimmed out, leaving the home side victorious.  The result marks a significant defensive hold for Tasmania, which maintained its unbeaten record on home soil in NBL27. For Melbourne, the loss serves as a rare setback on a Thursday night, a time slot where the team has historically dominated with 23 wins in its last 24 appearances. The game highlighted the intense rivalry between these two clubs, following their history in the NBL24 Championship Series.  The JackJumpers initially built a commanding 19-point lead by halftime, largely due to a dominant rebounding performance that saw them outrebound Melbourne 33-14 in the first half. Will Magnay celebrated his 100th game by contributing 17 points and 12 rebounds to the effort. Despite trailing 52-35 at the break, United surged back behind the efforts of Josh Oduro, who finished with 22 points, and Joe Ingles, who added 18. Melbourne chipped away at the deficit throughout the second half, narrowing the margin to 14 points by the final break before forcing the dramatic fourth-quarter finish. Tasmania coach Scott Roth praised Armstrong’s toughness and grittiness following the win, describing the performance as a reflection of the team's character in a high-stakes, foul-ridden matchup.

article.headline: Australia scraps credit card surcharges as banks slash rewards and hike fees
article.summary: Starting October 1, Australia’s Reserve Bank has banned checkout surcharges on card payments, a move aimed at saving consumers $1.6 billion annually.
article.body:
Customers stand to save $1.6 billion each year now that extra checkout surcharges for debit, prepaid, and credit card purchases have been removed. This nationwide reform enforced by the Reserve Bank of Australia covers transactions made on Visa, Mastercard, eftpos, and American Express, effectively eliminating surprise fees at the point of sale.

While the elimination of surcharges provides price transparency for consumers, the change is forcing a widespread reshuffling of credit card economics. Because the Reserve Bank is simultaneously lowering the cap on interchange fees that stores pay to banks, financial institutions are aggressively looking to recoup lost revenue. Financial literacy expert Nicole Pedersen-McKinnon warns that this has triggered a massive clawback of card perks, including reduced earn rates for frequent flyer points and the curbing of complimentary services like travel insurance.

For businesses, the transition presents a different challenge. Many cafe owners and merchants, faced with the inability to pass on individual processing fees, are opting to increase base prices to cover their overheads. For instance, some businesses report that rising supplier costs and staff wage increases, combined with the new regulations, have prompted immediate price hikes on everyday items. Experts note that consumers must now pay closer attention to notices from their banks regarding changes to annual fees and interest rates.

The Reserve Bank anticipates that the policy will eventually lead to lower overall costs for shoppers as reduced merchant fees filter through the economy. Canstar data insights director Sally Tindall emphasized that the policy aims to ensure shelf prices match the final amount paid at checkout. Customers are advised to monitor official communications from their banks, as providers are required to disclose any significant adjustments to card products.

article.headline: Gears of War: E-Day Campaign Plunges Players Into Brutal Locust Invasion
article.summary: The Coalition releases Gears of War: E-Day, a prequel set 14 years before the original game, featuring a campaign centered on Marcus Fenix and Dom Santiago.
article.body:
Watching the city of Kalona fall in real time while human defense attempts are thwarted by the Locust horde establishes the enemy as a true, unrelenting threat. The experience is defined by an overwhelming sense of helplessness; despite playing as an armored-and-armed-to-the-teeth soldier, there is no end in sight and no clear salvation for humanity as the ground literally opens up to reveal the invading forces.

For fans of the franchise, this release marks the return of protagonists Marcus Fenix and Dom Santiago to the spotlight. According to Game Informer, the campaign differentiates itself through an immediate horror tone, contrasting the intensity of a standout airstrip shootout with quieter, less-curated exploration elements across the city streets of Kalona. The game serves as a prequel to the original trilogy, focusing on the pivotal moment when the Locusts first emerge following the conclusion of the Pendulum Wars.

Beyond the narrative, the title is built on Unreal Engine 5 to showcase advanced technical capabilities. TechPowerUp reports that the game utilizes high-end graphical features, including RTX Mega Geometry, ray tracing, and multiple upscaling options such as DLSS 4.5, FSR 4, and XeSS. These technologies allow the game to run across a wide range of modern graphics hardware, with benchmark tests covering 35 different GPUs.

While the campaign has drawn early praise for its set-pieces and atmosphere, the full breadth of the release remains to be seen. Game Informer notes that the multiplayer components have not yet been experienced or evaluated, leaving that portion of The Coalition's latest project as an open question for players diving into the new title.

article.headline: Thulani Mabaso storms back with reserve team in dramatic Soweto Derby win
article.summary: Kaizer Chiefs midfielder Thulani Mabaso returned to competitive action following a long-term injury during a 3-2 victory over Orlando Pirates.
article.body:
Thulani Mabaso made his long-awaited return to the pitch in a high-stakes youth Soweto Derby, playing a key role as the Amakhosi youngsters edged Orlando Pirates 3-2. The match at Princess Magogo Stadium in KwaMashu served as the final step in the midfielder's recovery roadmap after he spent months on the sidelines recovering from a significant injury. 

For the Glamour Boys, the return of the left-footed technician provides a vital boost to squad depth as the club looks to integrate the talent back into the senior setup. Mabaso, who was promoted to the first team following a successful 2024/25 DStv Diski Challenge title campaign, offers a proven creative presence in the center of the park that the senior squad has been missing during his absence. 

According to Goal.com and FARPost ZA, the midfielder previously recorded seven appearances across all competitions in the 2025/26 season before his injury ended his campaign early. Sporting director Kaizer Motaung Jr confirmed that the playmaker's involvement with the reserve side was a successful test, noting that Mabaso is now rapidly approaching full match readiness. 

While the first-team coaching staff monitors his progress, the midfielder's participation in the opening fixture of the DDC campaign serves as a clear signal that he is nearing a return to senior duty. The club expects his fitness levels to continue rising as he transitions away from the reserve circuit and back into the primary selection pool for upcoming matches.

article.headline: Public Protector finds Mashazi guilty of improper conduct over unqualified appointment
article.summary: Former Ekurhuleni City Manager Imogen Mashazi was found guilty of improper conduct by Public Protector Kholeka Gcaleka on Thursday for appointing Ndumiso Gcwabe to a senior metro police role despite him lacking the required NQF level 7 qualification.
article.body:
Mashazi appointed Gcwabe as Deputy Chief of Metro Police: Security and Loss Control even though he held only a National Diploma in Policing and crime prevention certificates, falling short of the minimum requirement for the position.

The improper appointment matters because the role carried significant responsibility and a salary package between R1.6 million and R1.9 million annually. Public Protector Kholeka Gcaleka determined that Mashazi, as accounting officer, violated proper conduct standards by proceeding with the hiring despite the qualification gap.

The Public Protector's investigation, released Thursday, revealed that although the municipality verified Gcwabe's qualifications through a private service provider before the appointment, that verification proved inadequate. The finding came after a complaint filed on August 23, 2023, by Vukile Mlungwana on behalf of the Municipal Employees and Civil Servants Union.

Mashazi, who was arrested in July and released on R50,000 bail, faces charges of corruption and defeating the ends of justice. She has also appeared before the Madlanga Commission over allegations of abuse of power and protecting senior Ekurhuleni officials from accountability. The Public Protector noted that remedial action cannot be taken since Mashazi is no longer employed by the city.
